# agents/edge-critical-minerals/ — EDGE Critical Minerals Intel Agent

This agent runs the weekly EDGE Critical Minerals Intelligence Briefing pipeline. It is triggered by a cron job in `agent-job/CRONS.json` every Monday at 08:00 Ireland time.

## Files

- **`SYSTEM.md`** — Agent system prompt: identity, runtime environment, and workflow overview.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — This file. Context for AI assistants editing this agent.
- **`jobs/weekly-report.md`** — The full pipeline instructions executed each Monday. The cron job's `job` field references this file.

## Requirements

The agent relies on:

1. **Web Search** — Built into the coding agent (WebSearch tool). No external API needed.
2. **Google Drive Upload** — Uses OAuth refresh token auth. The `GOOGLE_DRIVE_OAUTH` secret (JSON with client_id, client_secret, refresh_token, token_uri) is stored as an agent job secret and auto-injected into agent-job containers. The target Google Drive folder (ID: `1ECFvfIafuyRqgU4fV9jFMt9GXzTRLO5T`) must be accessible by the authenticated Google user.
3. **Telegram Notifications** — Uses Telegram Bot API directly with bot token configured via webhook. Chat ID: `466297056`.

## Skills

The agent inherits root-level skills (`agent-job-dm`, `agent-job-secrets`, `google-drive-upload`). No agent-specific skills are needed.

## Cron Schedule

Defined in `agent-job/CRONS.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "edge-weekly-critical-minerals",
  "schedule": "0 7 * * 1",
  "type": "agent",
  "scope": "agents/edge-critical-minerals",
  "job": "Read agents/edge-critical-minerals/jobs/weekly-report.md and execute the full pipeline described there.",
  "user_id": "4ab4ba80-a095-4c07-bb61-3e3471545055",
  "enabled": true
}
```

Schedule: Every Monday at 08:00 Ireland time (07:00 UTC during summer).

## Pipeline Steps

1. Research (7 sections) using web search
2. Compute metadata fields (report_date, week_number, filename)
3. Build styled HTML report
4. Send report to Telegram via Bot API (sendDocument)
5. Upload to Google Drive (folder ID: `1ECFvfIafuyRqgU4fV9jFMt9GXzTRLO5T`)
6. Archive the HTML file in `agents/edge-critical-minerals/reports/`

🌍 Weekly Intelligence Report

EDGE Critical Minerals GeoIntel
Week 23  ·  2026

📅 01 June 2026 📊 REE · K-Th-U Prospecting 🌐 Web Researched 🇮🇪 Ireland · EU · Scandinavia · UK · Global

1. Funding, Grants, and Investment Opportunities

Top Picks for EDGE

1. EIC Accelerator — Boosting the European Critical Raw Materials Value Chain (€50M Challenge)
The EIC Accelerator 2026 Work Programme sets aside €50M specifically for technologies reducing European CRM dependence. EDGE's AI/ML prospecting platform qualifies under exploration and resource characterisation technologies. The blended finance model (grant + equity) provides up to €2.5M grant plus up to €10M+ equity investment — sufficient for TRL 6→8/9 commercial pilot deployment in a real exploration setting. Step 1 (short proposal) can be submitted continuously but should be filed 70–90 days before the target Step 2 cut-off.

  • Funding Body: European Innovation Council (EIC)
  • Stage: Accelerator (TRL 6→8/9)
  • Ticket Size: Up to €2.5M grant + up to €10M+ equity
  • Why EDGE fits: Direct CRM challenge includes exploration technologies; AI/ML platform for REE/K-Th-U prospecting is on-profile
  • Eligibility: Single SME (Irish SMEs eligible); must demonstrate innovation, risk, and growth potential
  • Deadline: Step 2 cut-offs: 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026; Step 1 continuous
  • URL: Zabala — EIC Accelerator 2026 Updates ↗

2. Horizon Europe — HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-22 (€36M Total)
Innovation Action for breakthrough materials and production processes reducing dependencies on critical and strategic raw materials. While the primary focus is materials substitution and processing efficiency, the call explicitly includes exploration-to-processing value chain integration. Opens 22 September 2026 with a 2 February 2027 deadline — ideal for EDGE to build a consortium with EU partners for a TRL 5–7 demonstration project linking AI prospecting with downstream processing.

  • Funding Body: European Commission — Horizon Europe (Cluster 4)
  • Stage: Innovation Action (IA) — TRL 7 expected
  • Ticket Size: €36M total (~€5–8M per project)
  • Why EDGE fits: Targets the full CRM value chain from exploration to processing; EDGE's platform provides the upstream intelligence layer
  • Eligibility: Consortium (3+ partners from different MS/AC); Irish entities eligible
  • Deadline: 2 February 2027 (opens 22 September 2026)
  • URL: Euramaterials — MAT-PROD-22 ↗

3. Research Ireland Pathway Programme 2026 — Up to €535K
Supports talented postdoctoral researchers across all disciplines to transition to independent research leaders. Earth science and critical minerals proposals are eligible under the STEM-led stream. EDGE could partner with a host Irish university (TCD, UCD, NUIG, UL) to co-supervise a Pathway awardee working on AI/ML for mineral prospectivity, covering salary, PhD student, materials, and equipment over four years.

  • Funding Body: Research Ireland
  • Stage: Early-career researcher transition to independence
  • Ticket Size: Up to €535,000 total direct costs over 4 years
  • Why EDGE fits: Direct vehicle to embed AI/ML geoscience research in an Irish university with EDGE as industry partner
  • Eligibility: Postdoctoral researchers hosted by eligible Irish research bodies
  • Deadline: Full proposals submitted May 2026; applicant response expected September 2026 — check for 2027 cycle opening
  • URL: Research Ireland Funding Programmes ↗

Additional Opportunities

  • UK National Wealth Fund — Cornish Metals (£52M Loan): The UK National Wealth Fund has committed up to £52M as a shareholder loan to Cornish Metals for reopening the South Crofty tin mine in Cornwall. Tin is classified as a critical mineral for solar, wind, and EVs. The project also secured US$210M in Nordic bonds. URL: National Wealth Fund — Cornish Metals ↗
  • UK DRIVE35 — Ionic Rare Earths Magnet Recycling (£12M): Innovate UK/APC has issued a £12M Offer in Principle to Ionic Rare Earths for a commercial rare earth magnet recycling plant at Belfast Harbour, targeting 400 tonnes/yr of rare earth oxides. URL: Belfast Telegraph — DRIVE35 funding ↗
  • Kernow Industrial Growth Fund (£30M — Cornwall): Cornwall Council's £30M fund over 2026–2028 targets critical minerals, renewable energy, marine innovation, and supply chain development. Open to applicants. URL: The Post — Kernow Fund ↗
  • Research Ireland Discover Programme 2026 (€300K): Education and public engagement projects with a deadline of 11 June 2026. While not exploration funding, it could support critical minerals outreach and education. URL: Research Ireland Discover Programme ↗
  • EIB Debt Financing for Strategic CRM Projects: The European Investment Bank is providing institutional debt (50–65% LTV) for CRM/REE projects under the CRMA fast-track framework, with €500M–€1.5B CAPEX capacity. URL: EuroMining News — Horizon Europe Mining Finance ↗

2. Scale-Up, Accelerator and Commercialisation Programmes

1. EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — Upscaling
For teams with validated technologies (TRL 5+) needing demonstration and market entry support up to TRL 8. Covers sustainable mining, circular economy, recycling, and advanced materials. Maximum project duration 2.5 years. The co-funding model gives access to EIT RawMaterials' extensive partner network across 50+ core partners and 200+ associated partners in Europe.

  • Organiser: EIT RawMaterials
  • Focus: Upscaling validated raw materials technologies toward market readiness
  • Funding: €500K–€2.5M+ co-funding per project
  • Deadline: 24 June 2026 (13:00 CET)
  • What they offer: Co-funding for pilot/demo activities, EIT RawMaterials partner network access, business coaching
  • URL: RTU — EIT RawMaterials calls ↗

2. EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — RIS Innovation Projects
Co-funding for early-stage innovation in EIT RIS countries, which includes Ireland. Targets exploration, sustainable mining, processing, reuse, and materials substitution at lower TRLs. Two submission windows available.

  • Organiser: EIT RawMaterials
  • Focus: Early-stage CRM innovation in RIS countries
  • Funding: €800K–€1M co-funded
  • Deadline: 24 June 2026 and 16 October 2026 (two cut-offs)
  • What they offer: Co-funding, business acceleration, EIT community access
  • URL: RTU — EIT RawMaterials calls ↗

3. EIT Jumpstarter 2026 — Pre-Acceleration Programme
Seven-month pre-acceleration for early-stage raw materials innovators. No equity required. Categories include Mining & Exploration, Recycling & Circular Economy, Metals, and Minerals. The 2026 edition closed for applications on 17 May 2026. EDGE should prepare for the 2027 edition given the strong fit with the Mining & Exploration category.

  • Organiser: EIT RawMaterials
  • Focus: Early-stage raw materials innovation (pre-startup)
  • Format: Online & in-person (Europe-wide)
  • Deadline: 17 May 2026 (passed — prepare for 2027 edition)
  • What they offer: Training, mentoring, EIT RawMaterials network, pitch competition, up to €10K prize (no equity)
  • URL: EIT Jumpstarter 2026 ↗

4. ESA Business Incubation Centres — Space Resources & Downstream Applications
ESA BICs across Europe (including Greece, UK, and others) provide孵化 support for startups using space technology for Earth-based applications. Companies working on satellite data for mineral exploration, remote sensing for CRM prospecting, and space-resource utilisation are eligible for funding, technical support, and business mentoring.

  • Organiser: European Space Agency (ESA) via national ESA BIC hosts
  • Focus: Space technology downstream applications including Earth observation for resources
  • What they offer: Up to €50K–€200K funding, business incubation, technical support, ESA network
  • Deadline: Rolling applications per regional BIC
  • URL: ESA BIC Greece ↗

3. Training, Workshops and Courses

1. KTH Summer School — Rare Earth Magnet Value Chain
Four-day summer school covering the complete rare earth magnet value chain from mining to recycling. Includes industrial technologies, magnet manufacturing, and end-of-life recycling. KTH is a leading technical university in Sweden with strong links to the Nordic mining and metals industry.

  • Organiser: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
  • Location: Ludvika, Sweden (on-site with online participation option)
  • Dates: 15–18 June 2026
  • Level: MSc/PhD/Professional
  • ECTS: 4 credits
  • URL: KTH — Rare Earth Magnet Summer School ↗

2. World Mining Congress 2026 — AI Short Courses
Two-day pre-event programme with three dedicated AI short courses taught by world-leading experts. Includes "AI in Mineral Exploration: Separating Hype from Reality" by Prof. Jef Caers (Stanford) and "Collaborative Intelligence in Mineral Exploration" by Fleet Space Technologies — directly relevant to EDGE's AI/ML prospecting platform.

  • Organiser: World Mining Congress 2026 / Peruvian Institute of Mining Engineers
  • Location: Lima, Peru
  • Dates: 22–23 June 2026
  • Level: Professional
  • URL: Global Mining Review — WMC 2026 AI Courses ↗

3. IRTC Basic Training — Raw Materials Risk Manager
Four-morning online course covering critical raw material risk identification, EU criticality assessment methodology, mitigation options, and regulatory frameworks. Certified in accordance with ISO/IEC 17024. Relevant for anyone in the CRM exploration space needing to understand EU risk frameworks.

  • Organiser: IRTC (International Raw Materials Training Centre)
  • Location: Online
  • Dates: 29 June – 2 July 2026 (09:30–12:15 CET daily)
  • Level: Professional/CPD
  • Cost: €700 regular / €560 students & EuroGeol holders (exam extra: €250)
  • URL: IRTC Online Training ↗

4. University of Milano-Bicocca — PhD Course on Critical Raw Materials and Environmental Impact
Multi-session online course covering REE, PGE, Li, and Co ore deposits, processing, life-cycle assessment, and environmental impact. Open to PhD students and interested professionals. Delivered via Webex by Dr. Alessandro Cavallo.

  • Organiser: University of Milano-Bicocca
  • Location: Online (Webex)
  • Dates: 6, 7, 8, 20, 21, 22 July 2026 (multiple sessions)
  • Level: PhD/Professional
  • Cost: Free (likely)
  • URL: UniMiB — CRM PhD Course ↗

5. SEG — Probabilistic Deep Learning Inversion for Critical Mineral Exploration
Two-day short course covering GANs, conditional VAEs, invertible neural networks, and normalizing flows for geophysical inversion applied to mineral exploration. Self-paced online format. Taught by Prof. Jiajia Sun (University of Houston). Prerequisites include working knowledge of deep learning and undergraduate geophysics.

  • Organiser: Society of Exploration Geophysicists (SEG)
  • Location: Online (on-demand)
  • Level: Advanced Professional
  • URL: SEG — Deep Learning Course ↗

6. Summer School — Energy Security and Geopolitics of Critical Raw Materials
Three-day hybrid summer school in The Hague covering geopolitics of CRMs, energy corridors, EU–Central Asia connectivity, and security implications. Suitable for building strategic understanding of the geopolitical landscape in which EDGE operates.

  • Organiser: Hague Research Institute / Humanity Hub
  • Location: The Hague, Netherlands (hybrid — online option available)
  • Dates: 24–26 August 2026
  • Level: BA/MA/PhD/Professional
  • Cost: €600 in-person / €300 online (early bird until 25 May)
  • URL: Humanity Hub — Geopolitics Summer School ↗

4. Conferences, Events and Partnering Opportunities

Must-Attend for EDGE

1. Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials Conference — 15–17 Sep 2026, Budapest
Covers LFP adoption, lithium and critical mineral demand, battery passports, black mass controls, and EU recycling/processing regulations. Attendees include miners, processors, OEMs, recyclers, policymakers, and investors. EDGE should attend to understand the battery raw materials demand side and connect with OEMs who are end-users of REEs and lithium.

  • Audience: 300+ professionals across the battery raw materials value chain
  • Why attend: Direct access to offtake partners and investors; REE demand outlook for permanent magnets in EVs
  • URL: Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials ↗

2. Rare Earths and Magnets — Expanding European Capacities — 29–30 Oct 2026, Stuttgart
Organised by EIT RawMaterials, this conference focuses specifically on building European capacity in rare earths and permanent magnets. Includes sessions on mining, separation, alloy production, magnet manufacturing, and recycling. Features a Mercedes-Benz plant tour. Policy-heavy with EU Commission participation — strategic for understanding the European REE policy direction.

  • Organiser: EIT RawMaterials
  • Audience: Industry, policymakers, researchers across the REE value chain
  • Why attend: Direct relevance to EDGE's REE prospecting; networking with magnet manufacturers and EU policymakers
  • URL: EIT RawMaterials — Rare Earths & Magnets ↗

3. Mining & Minerals Hall (MMH) 2026 — 20–22 Oct 2026, Seville
One of Europe's largest dedicated mining gatherings. The 2025 edition drew 7,500+ visitors from 50+ countries. Covers exploration, mining, processing, and sustainability. Significant Latin American and Iberian participation. EDGE could present its AI/ML platform to an international exploration audience.

  • Organiser: MMH / AMINER
  • Audience: 7,000+ mining professionals, investors, government representatives
  • Why attend: Largest European mining exhibition; strong exploration technology presence; networking with Southern European mining companies
  • URL: Resources Review — MMH 2026 ↗

4. Resourcing Tomorrow — 1–3 Dec 2026, London
Europe's largest mining and critical minerals investment event, featuring the Critical Minerals Ministerial Roundtable (27 Nov) with government delegations from Australia, Canada, Saudi Arabia, USA, and more. The event attracts CEOs, investors, and government ministers. EDGE should prioritise this for investor networking and partnership development.

  • Organiser: Mines and Money
  • Audience: 1,000+ mining executives, investors, government officials
  • Why attend: Premier mining investment event in Europe; Critical Minerals Ministerial provides direct policy access; significant investor presence
  • URL: Resourcing Tomorrow ↗

Additional Events

  • IAGOD 16th Quadrennial Symposium — 30 Aug–2 Sep 2026, Porto, Portugal. Theme: "The Role of Geoscience in the Energy Transition." Critical minerals sessions including European and global perspectives. In-person only. Abstract deadline 15 March 2026, early bird registration 31 July 2026. URL: IAGOD 2026 ↗
  • Mining & Critical Minerals Europe Conference & Exhibition — 20–21 Oct 2026, London (during LME Week). Co-located with MMTA Critical Materials Forum. URL: Mining & Critical Minerals Europe ↗
  • SEG — Integrated Geoscience Signatures for Critical Commodities — 10–12 Nov 2026, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Multi-scale integrated geology/geophysics workflows for critical minerals (Cu, REE, Li, Au). Pre-event seminar for early-career professionals. URL: SEG Critical Commodities ↗
  • ECOMONDO — Earth Observation for Sustainable CRM Management — 3–6 Nov 2026, Rimini, Italy. Session on Copernicus and satellite data for CRM exploration, monitoring, and circularity. URL: ECOMONDO — EO for CRM ↗
  • 2nd EAGE Workshop on Enhancing Subsurface Practices using AI/ML — 1–2 Dec 2026, Daejeon, South Korea. Hosted by KIGAM. Topics include ML for seismic interpretation, agentic AI for geoscience, LLMs for subsurface analytics. Abstract deadline 10 July 2026. URL: EAGE AI/ML Workshop ↗

5. Research, R&D and Collaboration Calls

Top 5 Fits for EDGE

1. HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-22 — Innovative Advanced Materials Reducing CRM Dependencies (€36M)
Innovation Action targeting TRL 5–7 demonstration projects for breakthrough materials and production processes that reduce dependency on critical and strategic raw materials. While the primary call text addresses materials substitution, the value chain scope from exploration through processing creates an entry point for EDGE's prospecting intelligence platform as the upstream data layer informing material sourcing decisions.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 4 (IAM4EU & Processes4Planet partnerships)
  • TRL: 5–7 (IA)
  • Lead type: Consortium (3+ partners from different MS/AC)
  • Budget: €36M total (~€5–8M per project)
  • Deadline: 2 February 2027 (opens 22 September 2026)
  • URL: Microfluidics Innovation — MAT-PROD-22 Analysis ↗

2. HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-16 — Technologies for Innovative Processing of Raw Materials (€49M)
Largest single call in the 2026–2027 Cluster 4 Work Programme for raw materials. Innovation Action targeting TRL 5–7 for innovative processing technologies. EDGE could contribute the exploration targeting and resource characterisation layer within a broader processing-focused consortium.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 4
  • TRL: 5–7 (IA)
  • Lead type: Consortium
  • Budget: €49M total
  • Deadline: 2 February 2027
  • URL: EFFRA — Horizon Europe WP 2026–2027 ↗

3. EIC Accelerator — Critical Raw Materials Value Chain Challenge (€50M)
The most directly accessible funding for EDGE as a single SME. CRM challenge within the €634M EIC Accelerator Work Programme 2026 supports TRL 6→8/9 technologies. Blended finance: up to €2.5M grant plus equity. EDGE should target the 8 July or 2 September 2026 cut-off for Stage 1 submission.

  • Programme: EIC Accelerator (Challenge-based)
  • TRL: 6→8/9
  • Lead type: Single SME (can include partners)
  • Budget: Up to €2.5M grant + up to €10M+ equity
  • Deadline: Step 2 cut-offs 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026; Step 1 continuous
  • URL: Zabala — EIC Accelerator 2026 Updates ↗

4. HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-CIRCBIO-03 — Advanced Recovery of CRMs from WEEE (€10M)
RIA for scalable technologies recovering critical raw materials from waste electrical and electronic equipment. While the primary focus is on end-of-life recovery, the call includes characterisation and sorting technologies that could leverage EDGE's AI/ML spectral analysis capabilities.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 6
  • TRL: 3–5 (RIA)
  • Lead type: Consortium
  • Budget: €10M total (~€5M per project)
  • Deadline: 17 September 2026
  • URL: EuroAccess — CRM from WEEE ↗

5. EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — Upscaling (€500K–€2.5M+ per project)
The most immediate opportunity: deadline 24 June 2026. For validated technologies (TRL 5+) needing testing and upscaling. EDGE should assess whether its platform has reached sufficient maturity for a KAVA upscaling proposal. The RIS Innovation stream (also 24 June) offers lower entry barriers for Irish entities.

  • Programme: EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14
  • TRL: 5+ (Upscaling), 3–5 (RIS Innovation)
  • Lead type: EIT RawMaterials core or associate partner
  • Budget: €500K–€2.5M+ (Upscaling), €800K–€1M (RIS Innovation)
  • Deadline: 24 June 2026 (both streams); also 16 October 2026 (RIS Innovation)
  • URL: RTU — EIT RawMaterials calls ↗

6. Policy, Regulation and Strategic Context

EU — Critical Raw Materials Act Implementation Accelerates

47 Strategic Projects Designated Under CRMA (May 2026): The European Commission has formally designated 47 strategic projects across 13 EU member states, covering the full CRM value chain from mining through processing to recycling. Northern Europe dominates mining and early processing, while Southern Europe hosts battery-related assets. An additional 13 strategic projects were approved outside the EU, including rare earth projects in Brazil and graphite in Greenland. Combined investment across the 60 strategic projects is approximately €5.5 billion. Strategic status unlocks accelerated permitting, access to the €3B RESourceEU funding, and coordinated support from the European Critical Raw Materials Centre.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: Mining South East Europe — 47 Strategic Projects ↗

EU Stockpiling Initiative — Tungsten, Rare Earths, Gallium Shortlisted (May 2026): The EU has shortlisted tungsten, rare earths, and gallium for its first joint strategic stockpile. Talks are underway with major ports including Rotterdam for storage facilities. Ten EU countries are involved, led by Italy, France, and Germany. This is the first coordinated EU-level stockpiling effort for critical minerals, modelled on the US National Defense Stockpile. Magnesium, germanium, and graphite are under consideration for future phases.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: EuroMining News — EU Stockpile Planning ↗

Export Restrictions on Permanent Magnet Scrap and Li-ion Battery Waste (2026): Export restrictions on permanent magnet scrap and aluminium scrap are being implemented in Q2 2026. Lithium-ion battery waste and black mass exports to non-OECD countries will be banned from September 2026. Copper scrap may be added. These restrictions aim to retain processing value in Europe and reduce dependency on Chinese recycling infrastructure.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: Mining Journal — €3B EU Spend ↗

UK — Critical Minerals Strategy Advances

UK–US Critical Minerals MoU (February 2026): The UK and US signed a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding on critical minerals in Washington DC. The agreement covers joint investment mobilisation, priority project identification, and streamlined permitting. A Mining, Minerals and Metals Investment Ministerial is to convene within 180 days. The MoU complements existing UK bilateral agreements with Australia and Canada, creating a network of supply chain partnerships.

  • Jurisdiction: United Kingdom / United States
  • URL: UK Government — UK-US Critical Minerals MoU ↗

UK Strategic Targets (2035): The UK Critical Minerals Strategy targets no more than 60% of any single critical mineral from one country, at least 10% of annual demand from domestic production, at least 50,000 tonnes of lithium produced domestically by 2035, and 20% of annual demand from recycling. The strategy is backed by up to £50M in new funding. Over 50 critical mineral projects are now based in the UK, contributing £1.79 billion to the economy and supporting over 50,000 jobs.

  • Jurisdiction: United Kingdom
  • URL: Mining Technology — UK-US Agreement ↗

Nordic — European Rare Earth Hub Emerges

Fen Complex Resource Upgraded to 15.9Mt REO (March 2026): Rare Earths Norway's Fen Complex in Telemark has been reassessed at 15.9 million tonnes of rare earth oxides — approximately 80% larger than the 2024 estimate of 8.8 Mt and one of the largest rare earth deposits globally. The resource contains high-value neodymium and praseodymium for permanent magnets. Production is not expected before the mid-2030s due to permitting and environmental requirements. A proposed "underground invisible mine" design aims to minimise surface impact but increases capital costs.

  • Jurisdiction: Norway
  • URL: Caliber — Fen Complex Resource Upgrade ↗

Norra Kärr Mining Lease Recommended (March 2026): The Swedish Mining Inspectorate has recommended approval of Leading Edge Materials' Norra Kärr heavy rare earth project, submitting it to the Swedish Government for a final decision. The deposit is one of Europe's richest HREE sources (dysprosium, terbium) with an initial 26-year mine life and annual production potential of ~248 tonnes dysprosium oxide and ~36 tonnes terbium oxide. All government agencies involved have recommended approval.

  • Jurisdiction: Sweden
  • URL: MarketScreener — Norra Kärr Lease Recommendation ↗

Ireland — Research Capacity Building

"Metals for a Green Ireland" Research Professorship (UCD): Prof. Sarah Gleeson (UCD School of Earth Sciences) has been awarded a Research Ireland Research Professorship building a 13-member research group focused on critical mineral systems and exploration tools. The group is developing remote sensing techniques using EnMap, PRISMA, ASTER, and Sentinel-2 data for mineral mapping in sedimentary basins. This creates a direct academic partnership opportunity for EDGE in Ireland.

  • Jurisdiction: Ireland
  • URL: Research Ireland ↗

Research Ireland Strategy 2026–2030 Launched: The new Research Ireland strategy commits to 3,800 PhDs, 2,000 postdoctoral fellows, 50 spin-out companies, and €650 million in multidisciplinary research investment over the period. The green transition and climate action are named priority areas, creating a supportive environment for critical minerals research funding.

  • Jurisdiction: Ireland
  • URL: SSPC — Research Ireland Strategy 2026–2030 ↗

Geopolitical Context

China controls approximately 70% of global rare earth production and 90% of processing, creating acute supply chain vulnerability for the EU and UK. The EU's designation of 47 strategic projects, joint stockpiling initiative, and export restrictions on scrap materials all reflect a coordinated strategy to reduce this dependency. Restrictions on Chinese entities participating in EU-funded CRM research and innovation are being implemented. The European Critical Raw Materials Centre (operational early 2026) will coordinate joint purchasing, stockpiling, and market intelligence. These dynamics create sustained policy tailwinds for EU-based CRM exploration technology providers like EDGE.

  • Jurisdiction: Global
  • URL: Chambers — RESourceEU Analysis ↗

7. Action List for This Week

[HIGH] Prepare EIC Accelerator Stage 1 proposal for CRM Challenge (next cut-off 8 Jul 2026): Begin drafting the 12-page short proposal, 10-slide pitch deck, and 3-minute video. The CRM value chain challenge (€50M) is the most direct funding fit for EDGE's AI/ML prospecting platform. Stage 1 is a short-form submission that can be prepared in 4–6 weeks. Engage EIC coaching service for proposal support.

[HIGH] Assess EDGE platform TRL for EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 Upscaling (deadline 24 Jun 2026): With 23 days until the deadline, conduct a rapid TRL self-assessment. If the platform is at TRL 5+, prepare a KAVA upscaling proposal for €500K–€2.5M. If not yet at TRL 5, target the RIS Innovation stream instead (same deadline) or use the 16 October 2026 cut-off.

[HIGH] Contact UCD "Metals for a Green Ireland" group (Prof. Sarah Gleeson): The 13-member research group is actively building and has synergy with EDGE's AI/ML prospecting and remote sensing focus. Propose a research collaboration, co-supervision arrangement, or commercial pilot using EDGE's platform on Irish sedimentary basin targets.

[MEDIUM] Register for Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials Conference (15–17 Sep 2026, Budapest): Early-bird registration likely open. This conference provides direct access to battery OEMs and offtakers who are end-users of REEs and lithium. EDGE should attend to understand demand-side dynamics and identify commercial pilot partners.

[MEDIUM] Submit abstract for IAGOD 2026 (Porto, 30 Aug–2 Sep 2026): The abstract deadline was 15 March 2026, but check the official website for late-breaking poster submissions. The critical minerals session is a prime venue to present EDGE's AI/ML prospecting methodology to 400+ economic geologists from the global exploration community.

[MEDIUM] Register for Rare Earths and Magnets — Expanding European Capacities (29–30 Oct 2026, Stuttgart): This EIT RawMaterials conference covers the complete REE value chain from mining through magnet manufacturing and recycling. Early registration likely opens in summer 2026. The Mercedes-Benz plant tour provides direct exposure to end-user requirements.

[MEDIUM] Explore Research Ireland Pathway Programme 2027 cycle for EDGE-hosted PhD candidate: The 2026 cycle full proposals have been submitted (results September 2026). Monitor for the 2027 call opening (expected late 2026). EDGE could partner with an Irish university to host a Pathway awardee working on AI/ML for mineral prospectivity, with up to €535K over 4 years covering salary, fees, and equipment.

[MEDIUM] Monitor HORIZON-CL4-2027 calls for consortium-building (opens 22 Sep 2026): MAT-PROD-22 (€36M) and MAT-PROD-16 (€49M) both open in September with February 2027 deadlines. Begin identifying potential consortium partners from EIT RawMaterials network, Irish research groups, and European geological surveys. The 6–9 month preparation window allows for a high-quality proposal.

Monitor announcements from the European Critical Raw Materials Centre regarding stockpile specifications, volumes, and procurement timelines.

[LOW] Register for IRTC Raw Materials Risk Manager training (29 Jun–2 Jul 2026, online): If a team member needs to build CRM risk assessment expertise, this ISO/IEC 17024-certified online course (€700) covers EU criticality assessment methodology, regulatory frameworks, and mitigation strategies — directly relevant to EDGE's positioning within the EU policy landscape.

## EIC Accelerator 2026 — Critical Raw Materials Challenge: Deadlines & Key Details

### 📌 Challenge Name
**"Boosting the European Critical Raw Materials value chain"** — one of five thematic challenges in the EIC Accelerator 2026 Work Programme.

### 💰 Budget
**€50 million** allocated specifically to this challenge.

---

### 📅 2026 Cut-Off Dates (Full Proposal / Step 2)

Full proposals must be submitted by one of these **six cut-off dates**:

| Cut-Off Date | Day |
|---|---|
| **7 January 2026** | Wednesday |
| **4 March 2026** | Wednesday |
| **6 May 2026** | Wednesday |
| **8 July 2026** | Wednesday |
| **2 September 2026** | Wednesday |
| **4 November 2026** | Wednesday |

## Critical Minerals & Rare Earth Funding and Investment Opportunities in Europe (2026)

The European landscape for critical raw materials (CRMs) funding has been transformed by the **RESourceEU Action Plan**, adopted by the European Commission on **3 December 2025**. This is the flagship initiative building on the **Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA)**. Here's a comprehensive breakdown of opportunities.

---

### 🏛️ RESourceEU Action Plan — The Main Vehicle

**Total mobilisation:** **Up to €3 billion** over the next 12 months (from December 2025) to support concrete projects.

**Key targets by 2030 (under the CRMA):**
- **10%** of annual strategic raw material consumption extracted in the EU
- **40%** processed within the EU
- **25%** from recycling
- No more than **65%** from any single country

---

### 💰 Specific Funding Instruments & Amounts for 2026

| Instrument | Amount / Target | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| **InvestEU** | Up to **€2 billion** in investments | CRM value chain projects |
| **Innovation Fund** (2026 call) | At least **€700 million** | CRM supply chains & clean tech manufacturing |
| **Horizon Europe** (2026–2027) | **€593 million** | Circular economy, process innovation, substitution, R&I |
| **Battery Booster** | **€300 million** | Upstream raw materials for batteries |
| **EIC Accelerator** | **€100 million** (€50m blended finance) | Innovative, scalable CRM tech projects |
| **European Defence Investment Programme** | Undisclosed | CRM for defence value chains |
| **Global Gateway** | Undisclosed | CRM projects in partner countries outside the EU |
| **STEP** (Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform) | Up to **€1 billion** from Member States & regions | Strategic CRM projects |

> **Note:** Horizon Europe also has a dedicated **€300 million** mobilised for R&I investment in CRM under the 2021-2027 programme, with the 2026-2027 work programme adding €593M specifically for circular economy and new production processes.

---

### 🎯 Strategic Projects — Fast-Track Status

The **second call for Strategic Projects** under the CRMA closed recently with **160+ applications** received — 95 from within the EU and 66 from outside. Of these:
- **75 projects** target the **battery value chain**
- **21 projects** focus on **rare earth elements** for permanent magnets (vital for wind turbines, EVs, defence)
- Several relate to **defence applications**

**Benefits of Strategic Project status:**
- Access to guidance on private and public funding
- Priority attention from the RESourceEU financing hub
- **Expedited permitting** procedures (single points of contact, streamlined environmental approvals)
- Greater certainty for potential off-takers

The first round (2024) selected **60 strategic projects** (47 in the EU, 13 in third countries). A new selection round is expected.

---

### 🆕 European Critical Raw Materials Centre (2026)

Set to be established in **early 2026**, modelled on Japan's JOGMEC. Functions:
- Market intelligence and strategic oversight
- **Joint purchasing** of strategic raw materials
- **Stockpiling** coordination (pilot scheme operational early 2026)
- Portfolio manager for diversified supply chains
- Financing coordination with private & public partners

Also launching: **Raw Materials Platform** — a matchmaking tool for demand aggregation, offtake agreements, and SME access.

---

### 📜 New Regulatory Measures Affecting Investment

| Measure | Timeline |
|---|---|
| **Export restrictions** on permanent magnet scrap & waste | Early 2026 |
| Export restrictions on waste lithium-ion batteries & black mass to non-OECD countries | September 2026 |
| **Aluminium scrap** export restrictions | Early 2026 (under assessment for copper) |
| Extended **labelling requirements** for products containing permanent magnets (hard drives, speakers, drones, toys) | 2026 |
| Mandatory **recycled content shares** in permanent magnets in products | Under CRMA amendment |
| Action plan for **domestic fertilisers** & recycled nutrients (targeting phosphate rock dependencies) | Mid-2026 |

---

### 🌍 International Partnerships & Investment Opportunities

The EU now has **15 Strategic Partnerships** with resource-rich countries, the latest being **South Africa** (November 2025). Key developments:

- **Negotiations launching with Brazil** — a major emerging rare earth frontier (projects in Minaçu, etc.)
- **Dedicated investment frameworks** for **Ukraine**, **Western Balkans**, and the **Southern Neighbourhood** (North Africa & Middle East — particularly phosphate rock, potash)
- **Global Gateway** — win-win investment projects in emerging markets
- **G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance** and **G20 Critical Minerals Framework** participation
- Cooperation on standards-based markets, traceability, and ESG

---

### 🏭 Two Priority Projects Already Funded

| Project | Location | Support | Mineral |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Vulcan Energy** lithium extraction | Germany | €250 million from EIB | Lithium |
| **Greenland Resources — Malmbjerg** | Greenland | Unlocking financial support | Molybdenum |

These two were announced as "quick-start" priority projects under RESourceEU.

---

### 🔄 Recycling & Circular Economy Opportunities

A major focus of RESourceEU. Key points:
- Current EU rare earth recycling rate: **<1%**
- With adequate feedstock, EU recyclers **could cover 20%** of permanent magnet demand
- **Export restrictions** on scrap will keep feedstock in Europe
- **Pre-consumer waste** (manufacturing scrap, trimmings, defective products) targeted for recycling incentives
- **Horizon Europe 2026-2027** dedicates €593M to circular economy + process innovation
- **WEEE Directive revision** (Circular Economy Act, Autumn 2026) will improve collection of end-of-life electronics

---

### 🧪 National & Regional Opportunities

Member States are also active. Example:
- **Sweden**: The **Swedish Energy Agency** programme "Swedish Metals & Minerals" is funding projects like **MAP-BIO-MINE** (biomining for REEs, decision Q2 2026). Companies like **Nidhogg Resources** are participating as industrial partners with project areas in Vintjärn and Sellnäs.
- **STEP**: The Commission urges Member States to channel up to **€1 billion** from the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform to CRM projects.

---

### 📋 Who Should Apply

- **Mining & extraction companies** (especially for lithium, rare earths, cobalt, nickel, manganese, gallium, germanium, molybdenum)
- **Processing & refining companies** (to build EU processing capacity — current gap vs. China)
- **Recycling companies** (permanent magnets, batteries, electronics)
- **Technology & innovation companies** (substitution, biomining, separation technologies, digital process models)
- **Renewable energy companies** (wind turbine manufacturers using permanent magnets, battery storage, solar)
- **Defence & aerospace** companies reliant on gallium, germanium, rare earths

---

### 🚀 How to Access Funding

1. **Strategic Project status** — Apply via the European Commission's CRMA calls (next round expected)
2. **Horizon Europe calls** — 2026-2027 work programme (€593M for circular economy & process innovation)
3. **Innovation Fund 2026 call** — At least €700M for CRM & clean tech
4. **EIC Accelerator** — Blended finance for innovative CRM tech
5. **InvestEU** — Via implementing partners like the EIB
6. **National programmes** — e.g., Swedish Energy Agency, German Federal funding
7. **Global Gateway** — For projects in partner countries with EU offtake

Companies should prepare **strong ESG and sustainability cases** as these are prerequisites for funding.

---

### ⚠️ Key Risks & Considerations

- **China** dominates >90% of rare earth magnet supply and has imposed export restrictions on graphite, gallium, germanium, and rare earths
- The **US** (EXIM Bank alone announced $100 billion for CRM) is investing at a scale that eclipses the EU's €3 billion — competition for projects is intense
- **Bureaucracy** concerns — governance structures for the new European Critical Raw Materials Centre are still being defined
- Projects must demonstrate contribution to **EU security of supply** and **ESG compliance**

---

---

## 🔑 Key 2026 Initiatives for Critical Minerals Scaleup & Commercialisation

### 1. RESourceEU Action Plan (Announced Dec 2025)
The European Commission's flagship plan to secure critical raw materials (CRMs) — including lithium, cobalt, rare earths, and molybdenum. It builds on the **Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA)** and is designed to **fast-track projects from pilot to commercial scale**.

**Key 2026 milestones:**
| Initiative | Timing | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **European Critical Raw Materials Centre** | Early 2026 | Market intelligence, financing coordination, joint purchasing & stockpiling |
| **Raw Materials Mechanism (online platform)** | March 2026 | Matchmaking between EU buyers and global suppliers for CRMs |
| **Pilot stockpiling scheme** | Early 2026 | Coordinated EU-wide stockpiling |
| **Export restrictions on magnet scrap & Al scrap** | Early 2026 | Keep secondary raw materials in Europe for recyclers |
| **€3 billion mobilised** | Throughout 2026 | For strategic projects that can deliver short-term supply |

### 2. EIC Accelerator – Direct Scaleup Funding
The **European Innovation Council (EIC) Accelerator** is a key vehicle for **deep-tech scaleup and commercialisation** of critical minerals technologies.

- **Example:** **Mecaware** (Feb 2026) — won a **€2.5M grant + up to €10M equity** for its hydrometallurgical battery recycling technology (lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper). Their pilot plant in Béthune, France, starts end of 2026.
- **Horizon Europe 2026–2027** allocates **~€593M** for circular economy, process innovation, and substitution projects.
- **EIC Accelerator** has a dedicated **€100M** for innovative, scalable critical mineral technologies.

### 3. Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027 (Cluster 4 – Digital, Industry & Space)
Relevant funding topics for **commercialisation and scaleup**:

| Topic | Budget | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| **HORIZON-CL4-2026-01-MATERIALS-PRODUCTION-11** (Extraction tech) | €20M | Sustainable mining & extraction of EU CRMs |
| **HORIZON-CL4-2026-01-MATERIALS-PRODUCTION-13** (Secondary raw materials monitoring) | €5M | Resource classification, data on recycling streams |
| **HORIZON-CL4-2026-01-MATERIALS-PRODUCTION-15** (Innovative processing & refining) | €25M | Higher recovery rates from low-grade ores & waste |

### 4. 47 Strategic Projects (First Wave 2025) + Second Wave (2026)
- **47 Strategic Projects** were nominated under the CRMA in 2025.
- A **second application round** opened in **January 2026** — new projects can apply for strategic status, unlocking fast-track permitting (27 months for extraction, 15 months for processing).
- **Challenge:** Only 5 of the 47 projects are fully funded; 25 are still in pilot/demo phase. The **RESourceEU €3B** aims to close this gap.
- **Notable supported projects:** Vulcan Energy (lithium, Germany) – €250M EIB loan; Greenland Resources (molybdenum) – could meet 25% of EU demand.

### 5. International Partnerships for Commercial Deployment
- **15 Strategic Partnerships** with resource-rich countries (latest: South Africa).
- **EU–South Africa Clean Trade & Investment Partnership (CTIP)** — €12B investment package, roadshows in 2026 for bankable critical mineral projects.
- **Brazil negotiations** starting soon.
- **Dedicated investment frameworks** for Ukraine, Western Balkans, and Southern Neighbourhood.

---

## 📌 Summary: Pathways for Scaleup & Commercialisation in 2026

| Pathway | What It Offers | Best For |
|---|---|---|
| **EIC Accelerator** | Grants (€2.5M) + equity (up to €10M) | Deep-tech startups with TRL 6–8 |
| **RESourceEU / EIB** | Up to €2B/year in loans & de-risking | Large-scale extraction, processing, recycling projects |
| **Strategic Project Status** | Fast-track permitting, regulatory support | Projects aligned with CRMA priorities |
| **Raw Materials Mechanism** | Matchmaking & offtake agreements | Companies seeking buyers/suppliers or project finance |
| **Horizon Europe** | €5–7M R&I grants per project | Earlier-stage tech (TRL 4–6) |

**Key takeaway:** 2026 is the year Europe shifts from policy to **execution and commercial deployment**. The combination of the RESourceEU plan, EIC Accelerator, and the second wave of Strategic Projects means there are now **multiple, concrete funding and support mechanisms** for companies looking to scale up critical minerals technologies in Europe.

## RESourceEU Action Plan 2026 — Critical Raw Materials Centre & Stockpiling

### Overview

The **RESourceEU Action Plan** was adopted by the **European Commission on 3 December 2025**. It builds on the **Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA)** and aims to accelerate and amplify efforts to secure the EU's supply of critical raw materials (rare earth elements, cobalt, lithium, etc.). The plan was originally announced by President von der Leyen at the Berlin Global Dialogue in October 2024.

### European Critical Raw Materials Centre (launching early 2026)

The plan establishes a **European Critical Raw Materials Centre** in early 2026. Its functions include:

- **Market intelligence** — providing robust data on CRM value chains, primary and secondary markets
- **Financing strategic projects** — steering and financing projects using tailored instruments with private and public partners
- **Portfolio management** — acting as a portfolio manager for diversified and resilient supply chains
- **Joint purchasing and stockpiling** — coordinating collective procurement and strategic reserves

### Stockpiling (pilot scheme early 2026)

- A **coordinated EU approach to stockpiling** critical raw materials is being developed with Member States
- A **stockpiling pilot scheme** is set to become operational in **early 2026**
- The **Stockpiling Sub-group** of the EU Critical Raw Materials Board is already working on reporting and coordination of stocks
- The stockpiling efforts aim to protect industry from **geopolitical and price volatility**, and increase awareness of possible shortages

- **€3 billion mobilization** — up to €3 billion to be made available over 12 months for strategic supply initiatives
- **Permitting acceleration** — streamlined permitting for Strategic Projects (27 months for mining, 15 months for processing/recycling)
- **Recycling & export restrictions** — export restrictions on permanent magnet scrap and waste from early 2026; similar measures for aluminium and possibly copper
- **Target** — reduce strategic dependencies by up to **50% by 2029**
- **International partnerships** — cooperation with 15 strategic partner countries (South Africa recently added); negotiations with Brazil to begin

## Overview

The **CLIMATES programme** is a £15 million initiative launched by the **UK Department for Business and Trade** (via Innovate UK) as part of the **UK Critical Minerals Strategy**. It focuses specifically on strengthening supply chains for **rare earth elements (REEs)** and permanent magnets, from mining through to end-of-life recycling.

## Key Details

- **Total funding**: £15 million of public funding (announced February 2024)
- **Focus areas**: Rare earth elements, permanent magnets, circular supply chains
- **Funding competitions**: Split into Strand 1 (early-stage feasibility studies) and Strand 2 (mid/late-stage R&D projects)
- **Example grant**: £6.6 million awarded to 16 innovation projects across 40 organisations for the "Critical Materials for Magnets Competition" round

## 2026 Developments

As of **March 2026**, there are published case studies showing the programme's impact:

- **Ionic Technologies** — secured four CLIMATES projects, producing the world's first EV motor using 100% recycled rare earths. Their £85 million commercial recycling plant in Belfast is planned to be operational by **2027**.
- **Nanomox** — advanced its OIS® technology from lab to pilot-scale, raised £2.4 million seed funding, and is building a commercial pilot plant in the UK.

## Future Outlook

The programme has produced **Innovation Landscape Reports** (published in 2025) that identify opportunities for future R&D funding across the entire REE value chain — mining, mid-stream processing, magnet manufacturing, recycling, and novel materials. These reports are intended to guide further investment beyond the initial £15m.

## 2026 Update: Rare Earth Norway (Fen Deposit) – Europe's Largest Mining Project

Here's what the 2026 search results reveal about the **Fen deposit** in Telemark, Norway, developed by **Rare Earths Norway (REN)**:

---

### 🔑 Key 2026 Developments

**1. Resource Estimate Soars 81% (March 2026)**
- The Fen deposit now holds **15.9 million metric tonnes** of total rare earth oxide (indicated + inferred), up from 8.8 Mt in 2024.
- This makes it **Europe's largest known rare earth deposit** — far exceeding Sweden's Per Geijer (2.2 Mt).
- About **19%** is neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr), critical for permanent magnets in EVs, wind turbines, and defence.

**2. Norwegian Government Takes Over Planning (April–May 2026)**
- Prime Minister **Jonas Gahr Støre** announced the state will assume responsibility for zoning and permitting.
- This **fast-tracks** the project and removes the risk of appeals/objections halting progress.
- The government cited "security of supply" and "geopolitical importance" as driving factors.

**3. Production Timeline**
- **First production**: late **2031**
- **Target output**: **800 tonnes of NdPr** by **2032** (~5% of EU demand)

**4. Thorium Partnership (February 2026)**
- Rare Earths Norway signed a Letter of Intent with **Copenhagen Atomics** to supply thorium from the deposit for use in next-generation **molten salt nuclear reactors**.

---

### ⚠️ Key Challenges

| Challenge | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Environmental opposition** | 78 red-listed species (beetles, mosses, mushrooms) at the processing site; county governor objected to the planned location. |
| **China's market dominance** | China controls ~90% of global processed rare earths and can engage in price dumping. REN CEO calls for EU price guarantees. |
| **Permitting** | Extraction permit is secured, but an **operating permit** is still needed. |
| **Financial risk** | REN wants Norwegian state co-ownership to share financial risk and compete with Chinese pricing. |

---

### 🧪 REEsilience Research Project (2023–2026)
A €16M Norwegian research project is underway to develop **sustainable processing technology** for Fen, including:
- Zero-waste mineral processing
- Safe handling of naturally occurring radioactive materials (thorium)
- By-product development (including radiopharmaceutical uses)

---

### 🌍 Strategic Context
The EU's **Critical Raw Materials Act** aims for 10% of rare earth needs to be sourced from within the bloc by 2030. Fen alone could potentially supply **30% of EU demand**. Currently, **no rare earth mines are operating in Europe**.

> *"The deposit has the largest documented occurrence of rare earths in Europe. The Fen field could be of great importance to Telemark, Norway, and European security of supply and competitiveness."* — Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre

## China Rare Earth Export Controls & Critical Minerals Geopolitics (2025–2026)

The search results paint a detailed picture of a rapidly evolving landscape. Here's a synthesis of the key developments:

---

### 🗓️ Timeline of Key Actions

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| **April 2025** | China imposed export licensing on **7 rare earth elements** (including terbium, dysprosium, yttrium) — widely seen as retaliation for U.S. "Liberation Day" tariffs. |
| **July 2025** | Some restrictions temporarily eased after U.S. pushback, but the licensing framework remained in place. |
| **October 2025** | China expanded controls to **5 additional elements** (holmium, erbium, thulium, europium, ytterbium) with **extraterritorial reach** — items containing as little as **0.1% Chinese-origin content** require Chinese export licenses, modeled on the U.S. Foreign Direct Product Rule. |
| **November 2025** | The October controls were **suspended for one year** as part of a Trump-Xi trade truce at the APEC summit in South Korea. The suspension **expires November 2026**. |
| **January 2026** | China imposed **dual-use export bans targeting Japan** — blocking exports for military end-users amid a dispute over Taiwan. Heavy rare earth shipments to Japan effectively halted. |
| **February 2026** | U.S. launched **"Project Vault"** — a strategic critical minerals reserve. State Department convened a **54-country ministerial** on critical minerals. |
| **June 2026** | New **Mineral Resources Law implementing regulations** took effect, coordinating mining, processing, stockpiling, and emergency preparedness. |

---

### 🌍 The Geopolitical Landscape

#### China's Strategy
- **Near-total control**: China accounts for ~**60% of global mined supply** and **~90% of processing/refining capacity** for rare earths. For heavy rare earths (HREEs), China's processing dominance was **99%** as recently as 2023.
- **Weaponized leverage**: Export controls function as a diplomatic tool — restrictions on Japan followed a Taiwan dispute; earlier controls responded to U.S. tariffs.
- **"Permissioned trade"**: The framework remains on the books even when dormant — licensing apparatus has been built, giving China **perpetual leverage**.

#### Western Responses
- **U.S.**: Pentagon took a **$400M equity stake** in MP Materials with price floors and 10-year purchase commitments. $1.6B committed to USA Rare Earth. **"Project Vault"** creates a strategic minerals reserve.
- **EU**: Critical Raw Materials Act; proposed restrictions on **permanent magnet scrap/waste exports** to build domestic recycling.
- **G7**: Discussing **price floors** for rare earths — an admission that resilience requires government-backed pricing to make non-Chinese production viable.

#### Supply Chain Bottlenecks
- **Heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium, yttrium)** are the critical pinch point — essential for high-performance magnets in defense, aerospace, EV motors, and robotics.
- Exports of these key elements are running at **41–49% of pre-restriction levels**.
- Yttrium prices have risen roughly **15-fold** since controls took effect.
- The only non-Chinese heavy rare earth refinery (in Vietnam) is offline due to a tax dispute.
- **No significant alternative supply** expected before **2027** at the earliest.

---

### ⚖️ Legal & Market Implications

- **Extraterritorial controls**: China's rules now apply to foreign producers using Chinese materials or equipment — creating overlapping compliance obligations with U.S. export controls.
- **Investment treaty exposure**: Export bans and quota systems are increasingly tested against bilateral investment treaties (indirect expropriation, fair and equitable treatment claims).
- **Force majeure disputes**: Export bans/quota systems are triggering force majeure declarations under offtake contracts — disputes already in arbitration.
- **Market bifurcation**: Two pricing tracks emerging — Chinese domestic prices vs. ex-China premiums, with calls for **new Western pricing benchmarks**.

---

### 🔮 Outlook

- **November 2026 deadline**: The one-year suspension of October 2025 controls expires — unless a new U.S.-China agreement is reached, the broader extraterritorial framework snaps back.
- **Structural dependency persists**: Non-Chinese supply chain buildout (mine-to-magnet) remains years away. $520M in U.S. rare earth investments were announced in Q2 2025 alone, but operational capacity takes years.
- **Resource nationalism rising**: DRC cobalt quotas, Vietnam's rare earth export ban, Indonesia's nickel ore ban — China's approach is part of a broader global trend of critical minerals being framed as **national security assets** rather than market commodities.

---

Sources: S&P Global (Jan 2026), Gibson Dunn (June 2026), AP/Reuters, CSIS, BMI/Fitch, South China Morning Post, Global Times, Economic Times.

## SEG Integrated Geoscience Signatures for Critical Commodities 2026 – Jeddah

The **Society of Exploration Geophysicists (SEG)** is hosting a workshop titled **"Integrated Geoscience Signatures for Critical Commodities: Acquisition | Processing | Interpretation"** in **Jeddah, Saudi Arabia**, from **10–12 November 2026**.

### Key Details:

- **Date:** 10–12 November 2026
- **Location:** Jeddah, Saudi Arabia
- **Organizer:** Society of Exploration Geophysicists (SEG)

### Background & Context:
The workshop is aligned with **Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030**, which places mining at the center of long-term economic transformation. It focuses on critical commodities including **gold, copper, rare earth elements, and battery-critical minerals such as lithium**. The Arabian Peninsula is noted as one of the world's most under-explored mineral provinces.

### Objectives:
The workshop emphasizes the **integration of geology and geophysics within a mineral systems framework**, rather than focusing on individual datasets in isolation. Key goals include:
- Strengthening knowledge of targeted mineral systems
- Improving structural and alteration resolution
- Increasing drilling confidence
- Reducing exploration and financial risk
- Applying scalable, cost-efficient acquisition strategies for Saudi terrains

### Target Audience:
- Exploration geologists, geophysicists, and mining professionals
- Mineral exploration service providers and technology developers
- Researchers and graduate students
- Early-career professionals (via a dedicated Pre-Event Seminar)

### Technical Committee (Co-chairs):
- **Naser S Jahdali** – Saudi Geological Survey
- **Junior Potgieter** – Viridien
- **Taqi Al Yousuf** – Aramco
- **Mohammed Gad** – Technical Development Solutions (TDS)
- **Catherine Truffert** – IRIS Instruments (SEG Convener)

The full committee includes over 25 members from organizations such as KAUST, Fugro, SLB, SRK, BGP, the Geological Survey of Finland, and many others.

# Norra Kärr Heavy Rare Earth Project — 2026 Mining Lease Update

Here's a comprehensive summary of the latest developments for the Norra Kärr heavy rare earth elements (HREE) project in Sweden, based on news from **March and April 2026**:

## 🚀 Major Milestone: Mining Inspectorate Recommends Approval (March 10, 2026)

The Swedish Mining Inspectorate (Bergsstaten) has **recommended approval** of the Exploitation Concession (mining lease) for Norra Kärr and **submitted the application to the Swedish Government for a final decision**. This followed positive endorsements from the County Administrative Boards (CABs) of Jönköping and Östergötland in December 2025.

### Key facts from the recommendation:
- **Norra Kärr is a globally significant source of HREEs**, with additional economic value from industrial minerals like nepheline syenite.
- **Estimated annual production**: ~248 tonnes of Dysprosium oxide and ~36 tonnes of Terbium oxide over an initial **26-year mine life** — covering only 30% of the currently defined resource.
- Dysprosium and Terbium are critical for permanent magnets used in **electric vehicles, wind turbines, and military applications**.
- The Swedish Geological Survey (SGU) has stated it is **"one of Europe's richest deposits"** for HREEs.
- Europe currently relies **almost exclusively on China** for HREE imports.

## 📋 Status Update: Swedish Government Yet to Decide (April 19, 2026)

In a follow-up update, the company stated that **every government agency involved in the permitting process has recommended approval** — but the **final decision is now with the Swedish Government**. The company has opened formal communications with the relevant ministry.

Other notable April developments:
- **Directors exercised options**, injecting approximately **CAD $788,000** in new capital into the company.
- An investor relations consultancy (Boofel Enterprises Ltd) was engaged to support capital markets positioning.

## 🧪 Processing Partnership

Leading Edge Materials also signed a **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** with **Ascension Earth Resources** to test innovative proprietary processing technology on eudialyte mineral samples from Norra Kärr, aiming to improve HREE extraction and recovery.

## Bottom Line

The Norra Kärr project has cleared every regulatory hurdle so far (CABs, Mining Inspectorate), all recommending approval. The **final decision rests with the Swedish Government**, and the company's CEO, Kurt Budge, has called an Exploitation Concession a potential **"game changer"** that would de-risk the project and enable acceleration toward construction and production.

This followed positive endorsements from the County Administrative Boards (CABs) of Jönköping and Östergötland in December 2025.

### Key facts from the recommendation:
- **Norra Kärr is a globally significant source of HREEs**, with additional economic value from industrial minerals like nepheline syenite.
- **Estimated annual production**: ~248 tonnes of Dysprosium oxide and ~36 tonnes of Terbium oxide over an initial **26-year mine life** — covering only 30% of the currently defined resource.
- Dysprosium and Terbium are critical for permanent magnets used in **electric vehicles, wind turbines, and military applications**.
- The Swedish Geological Survey (SGU) has stated it is **"one of Europe's richest deposits"** for HREEs.
- Europe currently relies **almost exclusively on China** for HREE imports.

## 📋 Status Update: Swedish Government Yet to Decide (April 19, 2026)

In a follow-up update, the company stated that **every government agency involved in the permitting process has recommended approval** — but the **final decision is now with the Swedish Government**. The company has opened formal communications with the relevant ministry.

Other notable April developments:
- **Directors exercised options**, injecting approximately **CAD $788,000** in new capital into the company.
- An investor relations consultancy (Boofel Enterprises Ltd) was engaged to support capital markets positioning.

## 🧪 Processing Partnership

Leading Edge Materials also signed a **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** with **Ascension Earth Resources** to test innovative proprietary processing technology on eudialyte mineral samples from Norra Kärr, aiming to improve HREE extraction and recovery.

## Bottom Line

The Norra Kärr project has cleared every regulatory hurdle so far (CABs, Mining Inspectorate), all recommending approval. The **final decision rests with the Swedish Government**, and the company's CEO, Kurt Budge, has called an Exploitation Concession a potential **"game changer"** that would de-risk the project and enable acceleration toward construction and production.

Here's a summary of the search results regarding the **EU defence critical minerals strategic stockpile — with a focus on rare earth elements and 2026 plans**:

## Key Developments

### 1. RESourceEU Action Plan (adopted December 2025)
The European Commission adopted the **RESourceEU Action Plan** on 3 December 2025, building on the 2024 Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA). This plan accelerates efforts to secure supply of critical raw materials — especially **rare earth elements, cobalt, lithium, tungsten, and gallium** — which are vital for defence, semiconductors, automotive, aerospace, and the energy transition.

### 2. Stockpiling Pilot — Operational from Early 2026
- A **European Critical Raw Materials Centre** is being set up in early 2026 to provide market intelligence, steer financing, and handle **joint purchasing and stockpiling**.
- A **pilot stockpiling scheme** became operational in **early 2026**.
- **Initial shortlisted minerals** for the first coordinated reserve include: **tungsten, rare earths, and gallium**, with **magnesium, germanium, and graphite** also under consideration.
- Most of these materials appear on **NATO's list of 12 elements critical to defence procurement**.

### 3. Rationale — Geopolitical & Defence Drivers
- **China's export restrictions** on rare-earth magnets and related raw materials (announced in late 2025) triggered urgent action, as China dominates global supply chains.
- The EU aims to reduce dependency on any single foreign supplier by **30–50% by 2029** for batteries, rare earths, and defence-critical raw materials.
- The plan is part of a broader "Europe's independence moment," with Ursula von der Leyen stating Europe must "fight for its place" amid geopolitical realignment.

### 4. Financial Commitments
- Up to **€3 billion** will be mobilised over 12 months to support alternative supply projects.
- The EU aims to fast-track **Strategic Projects** with the potential to reduce dependencies by up to **50% by 2029**.
- Member States can count stockpiling contributions toward their **1.5% GDP NATO defence spending commitment**.

### 5. Additional Measures
- **Export restrictions** on scrap and waste of permanent magnets (Q2 2026) to retain feedstock for EU recyclers, potentially meeting ~20% of EU demand for rare earth permanent magnets.
- **Demand-side measures**, including possible price floors to boost non-Chinese supply.
- **Public procurement reforms** prioritising diversified and resilient CRM sourcing.
- **Restrictions** on Chinese entities participating in EU-funded CRM research and innovation.

### 6. Logistical & Implementation Challenges
- The EU is in talks with major ports, including **Rotterdam**, for storage arrangements.
- **Permitting delays** and **community opposition** remain significant hurdles for mining projects within Europe.
- The **European Court of Auditors** (February 2026) found that EU diversification efforts have produced **"no tangible results"** so far, with domestic processing capacity declining due partly to high energy costs.
- **Recycling rates** for many critical minerals sit between **1% and 5%**.

### 7. International Cooperation
- The EU has signed **15 Strategic Partnerships** with resource-rich countries (most recently South Africa), and is in negotiations with **Brazil**.
- The EU supports the **Canada-led G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance** and the **G20 Critical Minerals Framework**.

## Key Takeaway
The EU's strategic stockpile for defence-critical minerals (including rare earths) is moving from planning to **operational reality in 2026**, driven by Chinese export controls and NATO defence needs. However, significant questions remain about **permitting speed, logistics, financing transparency, and the extent to which Chinese-owned downstream factories in Europe will still be permitted to buy these minerals**.

6. Policy, Regulation and Strategic Context

European Union — RESourceEU Action Plan Implementation Accelerates

RESourceEU Action Plan (Adopted December 2025): The European Commission's flagship plan builds on the Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) to mobilise up to €3 billion over 12 months for CRM projects. Key instruments include InvestEU (up to €2B), Innovation Fund 2026 (€700M+), Horizon Europe (€593M for circular economy and process innovation), and the EIC Accelerator (€100M for CRM). The plan targets reducing strategic dependencies by up to 50% by 2029. A European Critical Raw Materials Centre is being established in early 2026 to provide market intelligence, coordinate joint purchasing, and manage strategic stockpiling.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: EU Monitoring — RESourceEU ↗

Second Strategic Projects Round — 160+ Applications Received: The European Commission received over 160 applications for the second round of CRMA Strategic Projects, with the cut-off on 15 January 2026. Of these, 95 are from within the EU and 66 from outside. Applications include 75 battery value chain projects and 21 focused on rare earth elements for permanent magnets. The first round selected 60 projects (47 EU + 13 non-EU). Strategic status unlocks accelerated permitting (27 months for extraction, 15 months for processing), access to RESourceEU financing, and offtake certainty. Results of the second round selection are pending.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: 2EU Brussels — Second Strategic Projects Round ↗

EU Stockpiling Initiative — Pilot Scheme Operational Early 2026: Tungsten, rare earths, and gallium have been shortlisted for the EU's first coordinated strategic stockpile. The stockpiling pilot scheme became operational in early 2026 under the European Critical Raw Materials Centre. Ten EU countries are involved, led by Italy, France, and Germany. Talks are underway with major ports including Rotterdam for storage facilities. Magnesium, germanium, and graphite are under consideration for future phases. Member States can count stockpiling contributions toward their 1.5% GDP NATO defence spending commitment.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union / NATO
  • URL: Mining Digital — EU Stockpile ↗

Export Restrictions on Permanent Magnet Scrap and Li-ion Battery Waste (2026): Export restrictions on permanent magnet scrap and aluminium scrap are being implemented in Q2 2026. Lithium-ion battery waste and black mass exports to non-OECD countries will be banned from September 2026. Copper scrap is under assessment for future inclusion. These restrictions aim to retain processing value in Europe and reduce dependency on Chinese recycling infrastructure. EU recyclers could cover up to 20% of permanent magnet demand with adequate feedstock retained in Europe.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: Mining Magazine — EU Export Restrictions ↗

Scandinavia — European Rare Earth Hub Emerges

Norway Fen Complex — Government Takes Over Planning (April 2026): Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre announced the Norwegian state will assume responsibility for zoning and permitting of the Fen rare earth deposit in Telemark. The deposit holds 15.9 million tonnes of rare earth oxides (81% increase from 2024 estimates), making it Europe's largest known rare earth deposit. Approximately 19% is neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) critical for permanent magnets. First production targeted for late 2031. A Letter of Intent with Copenhagen Atomics will supply thorium for next-generation molten salt nuclear reactors. Every government agency involved in the permitting process has recommended approval. The deposit is one of Europe's richest HREE sources (dysprosium, terbium) with an initial 26-year mine life. An MoU with Ascension Earth Resources will test innovative proprietary processing technology on eudialyte mineral samples. The company raised CAD $788K through director option exercises in April 2026.

  • Jurisdiction: Sweden
  • URL: Globe and Mail — Norra Kärr ↗

UK–US Critical Minerals MoU (February 2026): The UK and US signed a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding on critical minerals in Washington DC. The agreement covers coordinated investment in mining, separation, and processing projects; joint project selection; streamlined permitting; and cooperation on pricing, recycling, geological mapping, and national security reviews of asset sales. A Mining, Minerals and Metals Investment Ministerial is to convene within 180 days. The MoU complements existing UK bilateral agreements with Australia and Canada.

  • Jurisdiction: United Kingdom / United States
  • URL: UK Government — UK-US Critical Minerals MoU ↗

UK Critical Minerals Strategy Targets: Backed by up to £50M in new funding, the strategy targets no more than 60% of any single critical mineral from one country by 2035, at least 10% of annual demand from domestic production, and 20% from recycling. The CLIMATES programme (£15M) supports rare earth supply chains with 16 innovation projects already funded. The UK critical minerals sector contributes £1.79B to the economy and supports over 50,000 jobs with more than 50 active projects.

  • Jurisdiction: United Kingdom
  • URL: UK Government — UK-US Partnership ↗

Geopolitical Context — China's Export Controls Shape Global Markets

China's Expanding Export Controls (2025–2026): China has imposed export licensing on 12 rare earth elements in two tranches (April and October 2025), with extraterritorial reach modelled on the US Foreign Direct Product Rule — items containing as little as 0.1% Chinese-origin content require Chinese export licenses. The October 2025 controls were suspended for one year as part of a Trump-Xi trade truce, with the suspension expiring November 2026. In January 2026, China imposed dual-use export bans targeting Japan, effectively halting heavy rare earth shipments. Yttrium prices have risen approximately 15-fold since controls took effect. Heavy rare earth exports are running at 41–49% of pre-restriction levels. China accounts for ~60% of global mined rare earth supply and ~90% of processing capacity.

  • Jurisdiction: Global / China
  • URL: S&P Global — Rare Earth Bottlenecks ↗

Western Responses to Chinese Supply Dominance: The US Pentagon took a $400M equity stake in MP Materials with price floors and 10-year purchase commitments. "Project Vault" creates a strategic minerals reserve. The G7 is discussing price floors for rare earths to make non-Chinese production economically viable. The EU's RESourceEU plan, stockpiling initiative, and 47+ designated strategic projects represent a coordinated Western response. The European Court of Auditors (February 2026) found that EU diversification efforts have produced "no tangible results" so far, with domestic processing capacity declining due partly to high energy costs. Recycling rates for many critical minerals remain between 1% and 5%.
