Jowitt) and Nanoscale Characterisation of Ore Minerals. Dates to be confirmed for 2026.

  • Organiser: Luleå University of Technology (LTU)
  • Location: Luleå, Sweden (likely on-site)
  • Level: PhD/Professional
  • URL: LTU — CAMM-CRM ↗

4. Conferences, Events and Partnering Opportunities

Must-Attend for EDGE

1. Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials Conference — 15–17 Sep 2026, Budapest
Annual gathering for senior leaders across the European battery supply chain — miners, processors, cathode/cell manufacturers, OEMs, recyclers, traders, policymakers, and investors. Topics include LFP adoption, lithium and critical mineral demand, EU battery regulations, battery passports, and black mass recycling. EDGE should attend to understand the battery raw materials demand side and connect with OEMs who are end-users of REEs and lithium in permanent magnets.

  • Organiser: Fastmarkets
  • Audience: 300+ professionals across the battery raw materials value chain
  • Cost: Super early bird €1,815 (expired 29 May); standard rate €2,145 from 30 June
  • Why attend: Direct access to offtake partners and investors; REE demand outlook for permanent magnets in EVs
  • URL: Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials ↗

2. Resourcing Tomorrow — 1–3 Dec 2026, London
Europe's largest mining and critical minerals investment event, featuring the Critical Minerals Ministerial Roundtable with government delegations from Australia, Canada, Saudi Arabia, USA, and more. Attracts CEOs, investors, and government ministers. EDGE should prioritise this for investor networking, partnership development, and understanding the institutional investment landscape for CRM exploration technologies.

  • Organiser: Mines and Money
  • Audience: 1,000+ mining executives, investors, government officials
  • Why attend: Premier mining investment event in Europe; Critical Minerals Ministerial provides direct policy access
  • URL: Resourcing Tomorrow ↗

3. Mining & Critical Minerals Europe — 20–21 Oct 2026, London
Co-located with LME Week and the MMTA Critical Materials Forum, this conference covers mining, critical minerals supply chains, technology, and investment. Strong UK government participation. EDGE could present its AI/ML platform to an audience of international mining companies, investors, and policymakers.

  • Organiser: Spire Events
  • Audience: Mining executives, critical minerals specialists, investors, government
  • Why attend: London-based with strong UK government participation; co-located with LME Week maximises networking
  • URL: Spire Events — Mining & Critical Minerals Europe ↗

4. Mining & Minerals Hall (MMH) 2026 — 20–22 Oct 2026, Seville
One of Europe's largest dedicated mining gatherings, drawing 7,500+ visitors from 50+ countries. Covers exploration, mining, processing, and sustainability. Strong Latin American and Iberian participation. EDGE could present its AI/ML platform to an international exploration audience and meet potential pilot project partners from the Spanish and Portuguese mining sectors.

  • Organiser: MMH / AMINER
  • Audience: 7,000+ mining professionals, investors, government representatives
  • Why attend: Largest European mining exhibition; strong exploration technology presence; networking with Southern European mining companies
  • URL: Spire Events — MMH 2026 ↗

5. SEG — Integrated Geoscience Signatures for Critical Commodities — 10–12 Nov 2026, Jeddah
Workshop focusing on multi-scale integrated geology and geophysics workflows for critical minerals (Cu, REE, Li, Au). Aligned with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 making mining a central pillar of economic transformation. The Arabian Peninsula is one of the world's most under-explored mineral provinces. Early-career pre-event seminar available.

  • Organiser: Society of Exploration Geophysicists (SEG)
  • Audience: Exploration geologists, geophysicists, mining professionals, researchers
  • Why attend: Direct focus on integrated exploration workflows for critical minerals; exposure to under-explored region with major investment
  • URL: SEG Critical Commodities Workshop ↗

Additional Events

  • Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Recycling Conference — 21 May 2026, Liège, Belgium (University of Liège – GeMMe). Industrial and geopolitical challenges of recycling rare earth permanent magnets in Europe. URL: GeMMe — REE Magnet Recycling ↗
  • IAGOD 16th Quadrennial Symposium — 30 Aug–2 Sep 2026, Porto, Portugal. Theme: "The Role of Geoscience in the Energy Transition." Critical minerals sessions. URL: IAGOD 2026 ↗
  • Critical Minerals Association UK — 4th Annual Conference — 2026 dates TBC, London. UK and allied critical mineral strategies, rare earths, policy. URL: CMA UK ↗
  • ECOMONDO — Earth Observation for Sustainable CRM Management — 3–6 Nov 2026, Rimini, Italy. Session on Copernicus and satellite data for CRM exploration and monitoring. URL: ECOMONDO ↗

5. Research, R&D and Collaboration Calls

Top 5 Fits for EDGE

1. EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — Upscaling (€500K–€2.5M+, deadline 24 Jun 2026)
The most urgent R&D funding opportunity. Supports validated technologies (TRL 5→8) in exploration, mining, and processing. EDGE should urgently assess platform readiness. The RIS Innovation stream (up to €1M) is a viable alternative if upscaling readiness is not yet reached. Ireland qualifies for RIS-enhanced funding rates.

  • Programme: EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14
  • TRL: 5→8 (Upscaling); 3→8 (RIS Innovation)
  • Lead type: EIT RawMaterials core or associate partner / consortium
  • Budget: €500K–€2.5M+ (Upscaling); up to €1M (RIS Innovation)
  • Deadline: 24 June 2026 and 16 October 2026
  • URL: RTU — EIT RawMaterials calls ↗

2. HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-22 — Reducing Dependence on CRMs Through Advanced Materials (€36M)
Flagship 2027 Innovation Action targeting TRL 5–7 demonstration projects for breakthrough materials and processes reducing CRM dependency. The value chain scope from exploration through processing creates an entry point for EDGE's prospecting intelligence platform as the upstream data layer. Opens September 2026 with a February 2027 deadline.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 4 (IAM4EU & Processes4Planet partnerships)
  • TRL: 5–7 (IA)
  • Lead type: Consortium (3+ partners from different MS/AC)
  • Budget: €36M total (~€5–8M per project)
  • Deadline: 2 February 2027 (opens 22 September 2026)
  • URL: Microfluidics Innovation — MAT-PROD-22 ↗

3. HORIZON-CL4-2027-01-MAT-PROD-16 — Technologies for Innovative Processing of Raw Materials (€49M)
The largest single call in the 2026–2027 Cluster 4 Work Programme for raw materials. Innovation Action targeting TRL 5–7 for innovative processing technologies. EDGE could contribute exploration targeting and resource characterisation within a broader processing-focused consortium. Opens September 2026.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 4
  • TRL: 5–7 (IA)
  • Lead type: Consortium
  • Budget: €49M total
  • Deadline: 2 February 2027 (opens 22 September 2026)
  • URL: EFFRA — Horizon Europe WP 2026–2027 ↗

4. EIC Accelerator — Critical Raw Materials Challenge (€50M)
Directly accessible single-SME funding. The CRM challenge within the €634M EIC Accelerator Work Programme supports TRL 6→8/9 technologies with blended finance (grant + equity). EDGE should target the 8 July or 2 September 2026 cut-off. The CRM challenge is one of five strategic challenges with dedicated evaluation panels.

  • Programme: EIC Accelerator (Challenge-based)
  • TRL: 6→8/9
  • Lead type: Single SME (can include partners)
  • Budget: Up to €2.5M grant + up to €10M+ equity; €50M overall for the CRM challenge
  • Deadline: Step 2 cut-offs 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026; Step 1 continuous monthly
  • URL: Zabala — EIC Accelerator ↗

5. HORIZON-CL5-2026-09-D2-01 — Producing Battery-Grade Materials Through Sustainable Processing & Refining (€28.3M)
RIA targeting sustainable processing and refining of raw materials for battery-grade production. While focused downstream, EDGE's AI/ML characterisation capabilities could support raw material quality assessment and resource classification. Deadline 15 September 2026.

  • Programme: Horizon Europe Cluster 5 (Climate, Energy & Mobility)
  • TRL: 3–5 (RIA)
  • Lead type: Consortium
  • Budget: €28.3M total
  • Deadline: 15 September 2026
  • URL: EFFRA — Horizon Europe WP ↗

6. Policy, Regulation and Strategic Context

European Union — RESourceEU Action Plan Implementation Accelerates

RESourceEU Action Plan (Adopted December 2025): The European Commission's flagship plan builds on the Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) to mobilise up to €3 billion over 12 months for CRM projects. Key instruments include InvestEU (up to €2B), Innovation Fund 2026 (€700M+), Horizon Europe (€593M for circular economy and process innovation), and the EIC Accelerator (€100M for CRM). The plan targets reducing strategic dependencies by up to 50% by 2029. A European Critical Raw Materials Centre is being established in early 2026 to provide market intelligence, coordinate joint purchasing, and manage strategic stockpiling.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: EU Monitoring — RESourceEU ↗

Second Strategic Projects Round — 160+ Applications Received: The European Commission received over 160 applications for the second round of CRMA Strategic Projects, with the cut-off on 15 January 2026. Of these, 95 are from within the EU and 66 from outside. Applications include 75 battery value chain projects and 21 focused on rare earth elements for permanent magnets. The first round selected 60 projects (47 EU + 13 non-EU). Strategic status unlocks accelerated permitting (27 months for extraction, 15 months for processing), access to RESourceEU financing, and offtake certainty. Results of the second round selection are pending.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: 2EU Brussels — Second Strategic Projects Round ↗

EU Stockpiling Initiative — Pilot Scheme Operational Early 2026: Tungsten, rare earths, and gallium have been shortlisted for the EU's first coordinated strategic stockpile. The stockpiling pilot scheme became operational in early 2026 under the European Critical Raw Materials Centre. Ten EU countries are involved, led by Italy, France, and Germany. Talks are underway with major ports including Rotterdam for storage facilities. Magnesium, germanium, and graphite are under consideration for future phases. Member States can count stockpiling contributions toward their 1.5% GDP NATO defence spending commitment.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union / NATO
  • URL: Mining Digital — EU Stockpile ↗

Export Restrictions on Permanent Magnet Scrap and Li-ion Battery Waste (2026): Export restrictions on permanent magnet scrap and aluminium scrap are being implemented in Q2 2026. Lithium-ion battery waste and black mass exports to non-OECD countries will be banned from September 2026. Copper scrap is under assessment for future inclusion. These restrictions aim to retain processing value in Europe and reduce dependency on Chinese recycling infrastructure. EU recyclers could cover up to 20% of permanent magnet demand with adequate feedstock retained in Europe.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: Mining Magazine — EU Export Restrictions ↗

Scandinavia — European Rare Earth Hub Emerges

Norway Fen Complex — Government Takes Over Planning (April 2026): Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre announced the Norwegian state will assume responsibility for zoning and permitting of the Fen rare earth deposit in Telemark. The deposit holds 15.9 million tonnes of rare earth oxides (81% increase from 2024 estimates), making it Europe's largest known rare earth deposit. Approximately 19% is neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) critical for permanent magnets. First production targeted for late 2031. A Letter of Intent with Copenhagen Atomics will supply thorium for next-generation molten salt nuclear reactors. Challenges include environmental opposition (78 red-listed species at the processing site) and the need for an operating permit.

  • Jurisdiction: Norway
  • URL: Energy News — Fen Deposit ↗

Norra Kärr Mining Lease — Awaiting Swedish Government Decision: The Swedish Mining Inspectorate has recommended approval of the mining lease for Leading Edge Materials' Norra Kärr heavy rare earth project and submitted it to the Swedish Government for a final decision. Every government agency involved in the permitting process has recommended approval. The deposit is one of Europe's richest HREE sources (dysprosium, terbium) with an initial 26-year mine life. An MoU with Ascension Earth Resources will test innovative proprietary processing technology on eudialyte mineral samples. The company raised CAD $788K through director option exercises in April 2026.

  • Jurisdiction: Sweden
  • URL: Globe and Mail — Norra Kärr ↗

United Kingdom — Critical Minerals Strategy Advances

UK–US Critical Minerals MoU (February 2026): The UK and US signed a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding on critical minerals in Washington DC. The agreement covers coordinated investment in mining, separation, and processing projects; joint project selection; streamlined permitting; and cooperation on pricing, recycling, geological mapping, and national security reviews of asset sales. A Mining, Minerals and Metals Investment Ministerial is to convene within 180 days. The MoU complements existing UK bilateral agreements with Australia and Canada.

  • Jurisdiction: United Kingdom / United States
  • URL: UK Government — UK-US Critical Minerals MoU ↗

UK Critical Minerals Strategy Targets: Backed by up to £50M in new funding, the strategy targets no more than 60% of any single critical mineral from one country by 2035, at least 10% of annual demand from domestic production, and 20% from recycling. The CLIMATES programme (£15M) supports rare earth supply chains with 16 innovation projects already funded. The UK critical minerals sector contributes £1.79B to the economy and supports over 50,000 jobs with more than 50 active projects.

  • Jurisdiction: United Kingdom
  • URL: UK Government — UK-US Partnership ↗

Geopolitical Context — China's Export Controls Shape Global Markets

China's Expanding Export Controls (2025–2026): China has imposed export licensing on 12 rare earth elements in two tranches (April and October 2025), with extraterritorial reach modelled on the US Foreign Direct Product Rule — items containing as little as 0.1% Chinese-origin content require Chinese export licenses. The October 2025 controls were suspended for one year as part of a Trump-Xi trade truce, with the suspension expiring November 2026. In January 2026, China imposed dual-use export bans targeting Japan, effectively halting heavy rare earth shipments. Yttrium prices have risen approximately 15-fold since controls took effect. Heavy rare earth exports are running at 41–49% of pre-restriction levels. China accounts for ~60% of global mined rare earth supply and ~90% of processing capacity.

  • Jurisdiction: Global / China
  • URL: S&P Global — Rare Earth Bottlenecks ↗

Western Responses to Chinese Supply Dominance: The US Pentagon took a $400M equity stake in MP Materials with price floors and 10-year purchase commitments. "Project Vault" creates a strategic minerals reserve. The G7 is discussing price floors for rare earths to make non-Chinese production economically viable. The EU's RESourceEU plan, stockpiling initiative, and 47+ designated strategic projects represent a coordinated Western response. The European Court of Auditors (February 2026) found that EU diversification efforts have produced "no tangible results" so far, with domestic processing capacity declining due partly to high energy costs. Recycling rates for many critical minerals remain between 1% and 5%.

  • Jurisdiction: Global
  • URL: Gibson Dunn — Resource Nationalism ↗

7. Action List for This Week

[HIGH] Urgent: Conduct rapid TRL self-assessment for EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 Upscaling (deadline 24 Jun 2026 — 16 days away): Determine whether EDGE's platform has reached TRL 5+ for the Upscaling stream (€500K–€2.5M+) or target the RIS Innovation stream (up to €1M) with lower entry barriers. Ireland qualifies for RIS-enhanced funding rates. If plausible, prepare a concept note immediately. The next cut-off on 16 October 2026 provides a fallback if the June deadline cannot be met.

[HIGH] Begin EIC Accelerator Stage 1 proposal for CRM Challenge (next Step 2 cut-off 8 Jul 2026): The 12-page short proposal, 10-slide pitch deck, and 3-minute video can be prepared in 4–6 weeks. The CRM value chain challenge (€50M overall) is the most directly accessible single-SME funding for EDGE's AI/ML prospecting platform. Step 1 is evaluated monthly — submit as early as possible to receive feedback in time for the 8 July or 2 September Step 2 cut-off.

[HIGH] Monitor Swedish Government decision on Norra Kärr mining lease: Every permitting agency has recommended approval. A positive government decision on the exploitation concession would be a significant validation of Europe's HREE potential and strengthen the policy case for CRM exploration technology investment. Track the decision timeline and use in EDGE's policy positioning if positive.

[MEDIUM] Register for Fastmarkets European Battery Raw Materials Conference (15–17 Sep 2026, Budapest): Standard rate is €2,145 from 30 June 2026 (plus 27% Hungarian VAT). Register before the rate increase. This conference provides direct access to battery OEMs and offtakers who are end-users of REEs and lithium, and is a prime opportunity for commercial pilot partner identification.

[MEDIUM] Identify potential Horizon Europe consortium partners for MAT-PROD-22 (opens 22 Sep 2026): With €36M total budget and a February 2027 deadline, begin mapping potential consortium partners from the EIT RawMaterials network, Irish research groups (UCD, TCD, UL, NUIG), and European geological surveys. The 3–4 month preparation window allows for a competitive proposal targeting TRL 5–7 demonstration linking AI prospecting with downstream processing.

[MEDIUM] Monitor the results of the second CRMA Strategic Projects round (160+ applications): The European Commission is expected to announce the selected projects in mid-2026. The outcomes will signal priority areas for CRM investment and may identify consortia or projects EDGE could partner with. Particular attention to the 21 rare earth-focused applications.

[MEDIUM] Track EU stockpiling initiative developments for REE market intelligence: The EU's shortlisting of rare earths for its first strategic stockpile will affect REE pricing and demand dynamics. Monitor announcements from the European Critical Raw Materials Centre regarding stockpile specifications, volumes, and procurement timelines. Price signals from coordinated stockpiling could inform EDGE's exploration targeting priorities.

[MEDIUM] Assess Research Ireland Pathway Programme 2027 cycle for EDGE-hosted PhD candidate: The 2026 cycle full proposals have been submitted (results expected September 2026). Monitor for the 2027 call opening (expected late 2026). EDGE could partner with an Irish university to host a Pathway awardee working on AI/ML for mineral prospectivity, with up to €535K over 4 years covering salary, fees, and equipment — a cost-effective way to embed research capability in Ireland.

[MEDIUM] Track Norway Fen deposit developments: The Norwegian government's takeover of planning and permitting represents a significant de-risking of Europe's largest REE deposit. Monitor the operating permit process, environmental impact assessment outcomes, and any EU Strategic Project designation. The Fen deposit's progress strengthens the European REE exploration narrative that supports EDGE's market positioning.

Scandinavia — European Rare Earth Hub Emerges

Norway Fen Complex — Government Takes Over Planning (April 2026): Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre announced the Norwegian state will assume responsibility for zoning and permitting of the Fen rare earth deposit in Telemark. The deposit holds 15.9 million tonnes of rare earth oxides (81% increase from 2024 estimates), making it Europe's largest known rare earth deposit. Approximately 19% is neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) critical for permanent magnets. First production targeted for late 2031. A Letter of Intent with Copenhagen Atomics will supply thorium for next-generation molten salt nuclear reactors. Challenges include environmental opposition (78 red-listed species at the processing site) and the need for an operating permit.

  • Jurisdiction: Norway
  • URL: Energy News — Fen Deposit ↗

Norra Kärr Mining Lease — Awaiting Swedish Government Decision: The Swedish Mining Inspectorate has recommended approval of the mining lease for Leading Edge Materials' Norra Kärr heavy rare earth project and submitted it to the Swedish Government for a final decision. Every government agency involved in the permitting process has recommended approval. The deposit is one of Europe's richest HREE sources (dysprosium, terbium) with an initial 26-year mine life. An MoU with Ascension Earth Resources will test innovative proprietary processing technology on eudialyte mineral samples. The company raised CAD $788K through director option exercises in April 2026.

UK–US Critical Minerals MoU (February 2026): The UK and US signed a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding on critical minerals in Washington DC. The agreement covers coordinated investment in mining, separation, and processing projects; joint project selection; streamlined permitting; and cooperation on pricing, recycling, geological mapping, and national security reviews of asset sales. A Mining, Minerals and Metals Investment Ministerial is to convene within 180 days. The MoU complements existing UK bilateral agreements with Australia and Canada.

UK Critical Minerals Strategy Targets: Backed by up to £50M in new funding, the strategy targets no more than 60% of any single critical mineral from one country by 2035, at least 10% of annual demand from domestic production, and 20% from recycling. The CLIMATES programme (£15M) supports rare earth supply chains with 16 innovation projects already funded. The UK critical minerals sector contributes £1.79B to the economy and supports over 50,000 jobs with more than 50 active projects.

Geopolitical Context — China's Export Controls Shape Global Markets

China's Expanding Export Controls (2025–2026): China has imposed export licensing on 12 rare earth elements in two tranches (April and October 2025), with extraterritorial reach modelled on the US Foreign Direct Product Rule — items containing as little as 0.1% Chinese-origin content require Chinese export licenses. The October 2025 controls were suspended for one year as part of a Trump-Xi trade truce, with the suspension expiring November 2026. In January 2026, China imposed dual-use export bans targeting Japan, effectively halting heavy rare earth shipments. Yttrium prices have risen approximately 15-fold since controls took effect. Heavy rare earth exports are running at 41–49% of pre-restriction levels. China accounts for ~60% of global mined rare earth supply and ~90% of processing capacity.

Western Responses to Chinese Supply Dominance: The US Pentagon took a $400M equity stake in MP Materials with price floors and 10-year purchase commitments. "Project Vault" creates a strategic minerals reserve. The G7 is discussing price floors for rare earths to make non-Chinese production economically viable. The EU's RESourceEU plan, stockpiling initiative, and 47+ designated strategic projects represent a coordinated Western response. The European Court of Auditors (February 2026) found that EU diversification efforts have produced "no tangible results" so far, with domestic processing capacity declining due partly to high energy costs. Recycling rates for many critical minerals remain between 1% and 5%.
